Metals & Mining Zimbabwe Appoints New Executive to Lead Growth Strategy

Metals & Mining Zimbabwe (MMZ), one of the country's key players in the extraction and processing sector, has announced the appointment of Tendai Moyo as Chief Operating Officer, effective 1 July. The move is part of the company’s strategic initiative to bolster its operational efficiency and support expansion plans amid a stable market outlook.

Moyo, who brings over 20 years of experience in African mining operations, was most recently Director of Production at ZimOre Resources. In her new role, she will oversee MMZ’s mining and processing activities across its gold, lithium, and chrome assets.

“We are excited to welcome Tendai to the executive team,” said MMZ Chief Executive Officer Samuel Chikafu. “Her track record in driving operational improvements and her commitment to sustainable practices will be invaluable as we pursue our next phase of growth.”

Zimbabwe’s mining sector is a cornerstone of the economy, accounting for over 60% of export earnings in 2023, according to the Chamber of Mines of Zimbabwe. Industry analysts note that sector stability and growing global demand for battery minerals have encouraged companies to strengthen their management teams.

“The appointment signals MMZ’s intention to stay ahead in an increasingly competitive market,” said energy and resources analyst Farai Mataruse. “Leadership with deep technical and local expertise is crucial for navigating regulatory and operational complexities.”

Moyo commented, “I look forward to working with the team to deliver on our ambitious targets while maintaining our focus on safety and environmental stewardship.”

No changes to current production guidance were announced.
